The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: together with.

notes: Always takes the dative case ('mit dem', 'mit der', 'mit den').
Used with means of transport where English uses 'by': 'mit dem Bus / Zug / Auto fahren' (to go by bus / train / car).

senses.definition: In the company of; together with.

examples.text: Ich gehe mit meiner Freundin ins Kino.
examples.translation: I am going to the cinema with my friend.
examples.emotion: casual and content, looking forward to the plans

senses.definition: Using a tool, instrument, or means of transport.

examples.text: Er schreibt den Brief mit einem Stift.
examples.translation: He is writing the letter with a pen.
examples.emotion: matter-of-fact and focused on the task

examples.text: Ich fahre mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
examples.translation: I go to work by bus.

notes: Mit always takes the dative case (dem, der, dem, den).
It covers both 'with' (in the company of) and 'by/with' (referring to the instrument or tool used).
Don't confuse it with 'bei', which usually refers to location or presence at an event.

faults.why: 'mit' is a preposition, not an expression.
Lacks the everyday sense 'having, containing' (e.g. 'Kaffee mit Milch').
